name: code-review
description: Review a committed GitHub diff on separate Standards and Spec axes with strict independent child contexts.

evidence.incompatibility: The upstream frontmatter advertises parallel sub-agents. In the Target Runtime Profile, @chrome-mcp is the concrete mechanism for creating independent child conversations. The runtime may claim the upstream behavior only when both running axes can be dispatched in parallel with direct GitHub access; otherwise strict review must stop.

transform.match: description: "Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes: Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to \"review since X\"."
transform.replacement: description: "Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes: Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Requires genuinely independent child-review contexts and reports the axes side by side; strict review stops when equivalent isolation or direct GitHub access is unavailable. Child reviews are spawned with @chrome-mcp and both axes run in parallel. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to \"review since X\"."

evidence.incompatibility: The upstream uses parallel sub-agents to prevent context pollution. In the Target Runtime Profile, @chrome-mcp is the concrete equivalent mechanism: create every required fresh child before sending either prompt, dispatch both axes in parallel, require direct connected GitHub in each child, and stop before any review begins if those guarantees are unavailable.

transform.match: Both axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.
transform.replacement:
Both axes run in **genuinely independent review contexts** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.

Use `@chrome-mcp` as the child-review mechanism. Before sending either review prompt, create all required child conversations with `@chrome-mcp`. Strict review can continue only when every child can use connected GitHub directly, and when both axes run you must be able to dispatch both review prompts in parallel. If `@chrome-mcp` cannot create or separately address all required children, if direct child GitHub access is unavailable, or if parallel dispatch is unavailable, stop strict review before sending either review prompt and state the missing capability. The pinned upstream workflow has no non-isolated fallback branch, so do not substitute sequential Standards and Spec passes in this conversation or label them as isolated child reviews.

evidence.incompatibility: The Target Runtime Profile has connected GitHub rather than the upstream local issue-tracker document/setup command. This translation changes only how the same issue/repository evidence is accessed.

transform.match: The issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.
transform.replacement: Use connected GitHub directly as the issue-tracker and repository-evidence mechanism.

evidence.incompatibility: The Target Runtime Profile is remote-first and cannot rely on local Git revspecs or commands. Connected GitHub can resolve committed refs, compare base/head with merge-base semantics, and expose the commit list while preserving the upstream fixed-point behavior and early failure.

transform.match:
Whatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.

Capture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.

Before going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.
transform.replacement:
Whatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.

Resolve the fixed point and the committed review head through connected GitHub. Compare the fixed point as base against the committed review head with merge-base semantics, note the commit list, and pin the exact head SHA that every child review must use.

Before going further, confirm both refs resolve and the committed comparison is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside the independent child reviews.

evidence.incompatibility: The Target Runtime Profile reads issue and repository evidence through connected GitHub rather than a local issue-tracker workflow or filesystem traversal. The upstream source-selection order and missing-spec branch stay unchanged.

transform.match:
Look for the originating spec, in this order:

1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.
2. A path the user passed as an argument.
3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.
4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report "no spec available".
transform.replacement:
Look for the originating spec, in this order:

1. GitHub issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, etc.), fetched directly through connected GitHub.
2. A repository path the user passed as an argument, read from the reviewed committed ref through connected GitHub.
3. A committed spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature, discovered and read through connected GitHub.
4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** child review will skip and report "no spec available".

evidence.incompatibility: The upstream step requires both sub-agents to be spawned in parallel and composed only after both reports complete. @chrome-mcp is the concrete Target Runtime Profile mechanism. Equivalent behavior requires creating all required child chats first, dispatching both running axes in parallel, treating retryable spawn/observation failures as recoverable while the run remains RUNNING, collecting until `barrier.satisfied: true` or a separate stop condition (genuine terminal failure, bounded timeout policy expiry, or explicit user cancellation), preserving direct GitHub access and isolation, and aggregating only after the authoritative barrier is satisfied.

transform.replacement:
### 4. Run both reviews in independent child conversations

Use `@chrome-mcp` to create a fresh ChatGPT child conversation for each axis that will run. Before sending either review prompt, create all required child conversations. When both axes run, the Standards and Spec children must be distinct and you must dispatch both review prompts in parallel. If `@chrome-mcp` cannot create all required child conversations, cannot address them separately, or cannot dispatch both review prompts in parallel, stop strict review before sending either review prompt and tell the user which capability is missing. Do not start one axis while trying to recover or create the other.

Treat child execution as a lifecycle, not as the initial spawn snapshot. `FAILED_TRANSIENT` with `error.retryable: true` is recoverable, not terminal; `EXTRACTION_FAILED` / "No ChatGPT worker result returned" can describe an uncertain browser observation while the worker is still alive. If the overall run is `RUNNING`, do not cancel it solely because `spawn_agents` reports a retryable transient child snapshot. Call `collect_agents(run_id)` and continue collection while the run is `RUNNING` and children are pending, dispatched, generating, observation-uncertain, or otherwise recoverable. A collector response with `failed: []` with pending recoverable children means the run is still alive.

Treat a child as failed only when collection reports a genuinely terminal failure (for example `FAILED_TERMINAL` / run `FAILED`). Separately, stop strict review when a defined bounded polling/timeout policy expires or the user explicitly cancels. Do not inspect, close, cancel, or aggregate any child early while it is recoverable, even if another child already produced a verified result. Aggregate only after `collect_agents(run_id)` reports `barrier.satisfied: true` for all required child reviews.

Every child must use connected GitHub directly, and the parent must keep findings isolated until aggregation. Give each child only the repository coordinates, the same pinned base/head refs, and that axis's inputs below. Each child must independently resolve the pinned head SHA and fetch the diff, commit list, and its required repository evidence through connected GitHub. Do not inspect or share any child's findings until all child reviews that will run have completed; aggregate only after that. Do not use sequential Standards and Spec passes in this conversation, shared chat history, parent-pasted repository evidence, or one child's findings as substitutes for independent child reviews.

evidence.incompatibility: The Standards reviewer is an independent child conversation rather than the upstream sub-agent. This terminology change names the equivalent mechanism without changing the axis.

The child cannot execute the upstream parent-local Git command. Passing repository coordinates plus pinned refs lets the child independently obtain the same diff and commit-list evidence through connected GitHub.
